user_prompt:
[Today, 6:05 pm] User: Quick one. I cut my hand quite deeply on the rusty edge of our outdoor bin about an hour ago. It's stopped bleeding. I can't remember when I last had a tetanus jab, probably at school, I'm 38 now. Do I need to do anything?

Write Ease's reply to the latest message.
response:
Yes, you should definitely have this looked at by a medical professional today (such as at an urgent care clinic, walk-in center, GP, or A&E). 

Because the cut is deep and happened on a dirty, outdoor surface, and it has likely been around 20 years since your last tetanus jab, you will almost certainly need a tetanus booster. Tetanus boosters are typically recommended every 10 years, or within 5 years for dirty or high-risk wounds, and are most effective when given promptly after an injury. A doctor or nurse will also want to make sure the wound is thoroughly cleaned and doesn't need stitches.

If you haven't already, gently wash the wound with warm water and mild soap, pat it dry, and cover it with a clean bandage or dressing while you arrange to get it checked out. 

Please take care and get that seen to soon!
